 Delhi High Court Refuses To Stay Ban On Non-Delhi Pre-BS-VI Vehicles From Entering Capital 
 Case Title : GURMUKH DASS KOHLI v. GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI AND ORS
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1055
 The Delhi High Court refused to grant interim relief against the Delhi government's decision to prohibit entry of non-Delhi-registered vehicles that do not comply with BS-VI emission standards into the national capital from November 01, to January 31.
 A division bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice on a plea challenging the restriction and directed that the matter be listed along with a related case on November 27.
 Delhi High Court Stays Termination Of JNU Professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam Over Sexual Harassment Allegations 
 Case Title : Angomcha Bimol Akoijam v. JNU
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1056
 The Delhi High Court stayed the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) administration's decision to terminate the services of Congress MP and professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam over allegations of sexual harassment.
 Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani issued notice to the varsity on Akoijam's plea challenging the termination order and listed the matter for hearing in January 2027.
 Delhi High Court Sets Aside CIC Order Directing HC To Disclose Data On 'Delayed' Judgments 
 Case Title : PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER v. P.D.GUPTA
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1057
 The Delhi High Court has set aside a Central Information Commission (CIC) order directing the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the High Court to locate and disclose details of cases in which judgments were reserved but not pronounced within two months.
 LinkedIn Doesn't Perform Public Function, Account Restriction Can't Be Challenged In Writ Jurisdiction: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title : Mayank Jain V/S Union Of India & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1058
 The Delhi High Court has dismissed a petition challenging the restriction of a user's LinkedIn account, holding that the social networking platform does not perform a public function or discharge a public duty and is therefore not amenable to writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
 Delhi High Court Keeps In Abeyance Its Order Directing Criminal Complaint Against 6 CBI Officers For Making False Statement In Court 
 Title: Sushil Dewan v. UoI
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1059
 The Delhi High Court has kept in abeyance its order directing registration of a criminal complaint against six former CBI officers for making a false statement before the court regarding correspondence with the administrative Ministry.
 Right To Education Doesn't Mean Right To Secure Seat In Course Of Choice Without Meeting Eligibility Criteria: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title : Suvan Yaduvanshi v. University of Delhi & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1060
 The Delhi High Court has held that the right to education under Article 21 of the Constitution of India does not extend to a right to secure admission in a programme of one's choice without satisfying the prescribed eligibility conditions.
 Justice Jasmeet Singh made the observation while upholding the University of Delhi's subject-mapping criteria for undergraduate admissions through CUET-UG 2025.
 Mere Website Accessibility Can't Confer Territorial Jurisdiction In IP Suits, Courts Must Draw 'Lakshman Rekha': Delhi High Court 
 Title: ABD MAESTRO PRIVATE LIMITED v. GREAT GALLEON VENTURES LTD and other connected matters
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1061
 The Delhi High Court has held that mere accessibility of a website offering allegedly infringing goods or services within its territorial limits does not confer jurisdiction to entertain an intellectual property infringement suit.
 Delhi High Court Refuses To Entertain PIL Seeking Stay On Sunny Deol's 'Suryaa' Release 
 Case Title : NACHIKETA BHATIA & ANR v. UOI & ORS
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1062
 The Delhi High Court refused to entertain a PIL seeking stay on the theatrical release of the upcoming film “Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak” starring Bollywood actor Sunny Deol.
 Anissia Batra Death Case: Delhi High Court Discharges Husband Of Cruelty, Abetment Of Suicide Charges 
 Case Title : NILLUM BATRA v. STATE & ORS And other connected matters
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1063
 The Delhi High Court has discharged Mayank Singhvi, husband of late flight attendant Anissia Batra, of charges of cruelty and abetment of suicide in the 2018 suicide case.
 Justice Madhu Jain held that the prosecution material did not disclose the essential ingredients of either offence.
 Delhi High Court Protects Actress Kriti Sanon's Personality Rights Against AI Deepfakes, Impersonation 
 Title: KRITI SANON v. BBE MARKETING INC & ORS
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1064
 The Delhi High Court has granted interim protection to actor Kriti Sanon against the alleged misuse of her name, image, likeness and voice through AI-generated content, sexually explicit deepfakes and impersonating accounts.
 Takedown Notices For IFF, SFLC Were Sent By Impostor, Not Delhi Police: X Corp Tells Delhi High Court 
 Title: Internet Freedom Foundation v. UOI and other connected matter
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1065
 X Corp (formerly Twitter) informed the Delhi High Court that the takedown notices sent to Internet Freedom Foundation and SFLC were by some impostor and not by the Delhi Police.
 X's counsel told Justice Amit Mahajan that a complaint has been filed with the Delhi Police to find the impostor and that no action is taken against IFF and SFLC.
 Delhi High Court Transfers Case After Lawyer Repeatedly Says 'I Cry My Beloved Justice System' And Walks Out Of Court, Calls It Misconduct 
 Title: ARJUN DEV BHATIA v. STATE NCT OF DELHI & ORS
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1066
 The Delhi High Court has transferred a case to another Bench after expressing strong displeasure over the conduct of an advocate who repeatedly remarked “I cry my beloved justice system” during a hearing and walked out of the courtroom.
 Delhi High Court Directs 'Doosra' Makers To Add Disclaimer Stating Film Doesn't Have Sourav Ganguly's Consent To Use His Name 
 Title: Sourav Ganguly & And v. Abhinay Deo & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1067
 The Delhi High Court directed the producers and directors of upcoming film “Doosra” to add disclaimer in the starting and end of the movie clearly stating that it is not intended to infringe the personality rights of former Indian cricket captain Sourav Ganguly.
 Justice Tejas Karia directed the producers to state clearly in the disclaimer that the use of Ganguly's name in the movie shall not be construed as an acknowledgement or consent to such use.
 Delhi High Court Exempts NCR-Based Court Staff, Lawyers From Winter Ban On Non-BS-VI Vehicles 
 Title: DHCBA v. GNCTD
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1068
 The Delhi High Court said that the court staff and lawyers will be exemption from the winter vehicle-entry restrictions imposed on vehicles registered outside the national capital and below BS-VI emission standards.
 Delhi High Court Decrees Amitabh Bachchan's Personality Rights Suit Against Multiple Defendants 
 Case Title : AMITABH BACHCHAN v. RAJAT NEGI & ORS
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1069
 The Delhi High Court has decreed Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's personality rights suit against multiple defendants, restraining them from unauthorised commercial use of his name, image, voice, likeness and other aspects of his persona.
 'Political Satire Can't Attack Dignity': Delhi High Court Orders Takedown Of AAP's Deepfake Videos Targeting CM Rekha Gupta 
 Case Title : Smt Rekha Gupta v. Aam Aadmi Party & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1070
 The Delhi High Court directed the removal of certain AI-generated videos, images and posts allegedly depicting Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta in a defamatory and demeaning manner, observing that political satire cannot be permitted to attack an individual's dignity.
